caption: Molten sealing wax is dripped onto the flap of an envelope and a metal stamp is pressed into the pool, and the wax sets hard with the stamped pattern within seconds.

sa.check: Molten wax is dripped onto the flap of an envelope.
A metal stamp is pressed into the pool of wax.
The wax holds the stamp's pattern.
The set wax looks dull rather than glossy.
The order is drip, press, lift, set pattern.

pc.expect: The wax is a thick liquid that mounds and spreads as it lands, takes the stamp's shape under pressure and sets as a firm solid that keeps it.
pc.fail: The wax runs off the envelope as thin as water; or the pool springs back to a dome as the stamp lifts; or the wax shatters under the stamp; or the set wax bends as the envelope is moved.

pc.expect: The stamp's pattern appears in the wax as a sunken print of the stamp's face and stays sharp after the stamp lifts.
pc.fail: The print sinks back and the wax ends smooth; or the print keeps changing shape after the stamp is away; or a pattern appears that the stamp's face does not carry; or the print appears before the stamp touches the wax.

pc.expect: The wax falls downward onto the flap and spreads out level in a pool, and the stamp comes down onto it.
pc.fail: The wax travels upward from the spoon; or the pool climbs the envelope's edge and stays; or the pool stands as a tall column above the flap; or wax lifts off the envelope and hangs.

pc.expect: Pressing shows: the wax spreads wider under the stamp and rises around its edge.
pc.fail: The stamp presses in and the pool's width does not change; or wax rises on a part of the envelope away from the stamp; or the stamp presses down to the paper with no wax squeezing out.

pc.expect: One pool of wax, one stamp and one envelope; the stamp stays outside the paper and the wax stays on the flap.
pc.fail: The stamp passes through the envelope; or a second seal appears; or the wax vanishes; or the envelope changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The envelope's paper, the stamp's handle and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The envelope's paper changes colour; or the stamp's handle changes shape; or items on the table rearrange.
